notes: AP tomato has two main crop cycles: Kharif (Jun–Sep sowing, Oct–Dec harvest) and Rabi (Oct–Dec sowing, Feb–Apr harvest). Madanapalli is the single largest tomato growing cluster in India with ~60,000 acres under cultivation.

seasons.name: Pre-Kharif Lean
seasons.description: Post-Rabi harvest exhausted. Pre-Kharif supply trough. Prices typically peak May–June.
seasons.procurement_advice: Lock in contracts early. Prices likely to rise through June.

seasons.name: Kharif Harvest Flush
seasons.description: Kharif crop arrives at mandis. Supply surge. Prices crash sharply.
seasons.procurement_advice: Spot buy. Avoid long-term contracts. Prices at seasonal lows.

seasons.name: Rabi Growing
seasons.description: Kharif supply winding down. Rabi crop still growing. Prices recovering.
seasons.procurement_advice: Start building forward coverage. Prices rising.

seasons.name: Rabi Harvest
seasons.description: Rabi crop harvested. Second supply peak of the year. Prices moderate.
seasons.procurement_advice: Good time for spot buying. Prices will ease through April.

seasons.name: Post-Kharif Transition
seasons.description: Kharif crop maturing. Pre-harvest period. Price direction depends on monsoon quality and NDVI.
seasons.procurement_advice: Monitor NDVI and arrivals closely. Mixed signals period. Use split strategy.

ndvi_thresholds.notes: NDVI readings are 2-month leading indicators of harvest volume. Values below 0.40 in growing months (Jun–Sep) signal supply shock risk.

major_risk_events.impact: Transport disruption, quality deterioration, 2–3 week supply gap
Occasional mandi closure (1–2 days). Minimal procurement impact.
Arrival disruption for 1–2 weeks. Price spike possible.
Accelerated crop maturity, short-term supply glut followed by shortage
